turns.t: Good morning, dear. I do hope I'm not wasting your time, I only came because my daughter said I must, I keep forgetting my tablets.
You're not wasting it. Tell me how that happens, forgetting them. ~

Well, I have the morning ones and the evening ones, and in the morning I get distracted, there's the cat, and the radio, and the phone goes, and then at night I find the morning ones still on the saucer.
How often would you say you miss them?
Oh, three or four mornings a week, I should think. I've written it on the calendar, but then I forget to look at the calendar!
You're certainly not alone. Have you had any falls lately?
No, no falls. I'm very careful with the stairs.
Any dizziness, light-headedness?
No, none. I'm steady as a rock, ask my daughter.
Do you remember what the tablets are for?
They're for my blood pressure, the two of them. High blood pressure, I've had it since my fifties.
Any allergies to medicines, that we should know about?
Penicillin. I came out in a rash, as a girl, and my mother said never again.
Thank you. Let me check how you're doing. Pulse and pressure, please. ~
Take whatever you need. ~
Pulse 68 and regular, blood pressure 148 over 84, temperature 36.5, oxygen 97 percent, weight 61 kilos.
Is that good, dear? ~
The pressure's a little high, which fits with missing doses. And your pulse is regular. Any breathlessness or chest tightness?
No, I walk to the shops and back without trouble.
That's good. Here's my thought. Two tablets, at two different times, is a lot to remember. I'd like to simplify it to one tablet, once a day. ~
One! That would be lovely. ~
I'm going to start you on ramipril, 5 mg once a day, for your blood pressure, and stop the other two.
And the old ones? ~
The pharmacist will take them back. And we'll get a pill organiser, a box with the days of the week, so you can see at a glance.
Oh, like my husband's, God rest him. That was a good box. ~
Exactly. Keep it by the kettle, so you see it when you make your morning tea.
The kettle. I never forget the kettle. ~
I'd also like to check your kidney function with a blood test, since you're starting a new tablet.
Of course. Can they do it today? ~
Yes, at reception. If you feel dizzy, or your face or lips swell, or you develop a dry cough that won't go, stop it and let us know.
Right. I'll remember that. Or Maureen will. ~
Perfect. Thank you for coming in. ~

symptoms.name: find the morning ones still on the saucer
symptoms.frequency: three or four mornings a week

clinical_actions.description: Start Ramipril 5 mg once a day
Get a weekly pill organiser; pharmacist to take back old tablets
Keep the organiser by the kettle
Stop ramipril and contact us if dizziness, facial or lip swelling, or a persistent dry cough
